docs.text: Driver PCA9685 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the NXP PCA9685 16-channel, 12-bit PWM controller. It starts the chip from any state with every output off, sets duty, phase and servo pulse widths, changes the frequency by the data sheet's sleep and restart sequence, finds chip resets and never refuses a switch-off, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings the bus up and moves bytes; it does the rest: the start-up from any state, the register framing with auto-increment, the frequency arithmetic, the sleep and restart sequence, reset detection and the bookkeeping of writes that may or may not have arrived. PWM controller PCA9685 NXP Function 16 outputs, each with its own 12-bit PWM (4096 steps) and turn-on delay, all at one frequency Frequency About 24 Hz to 1526 Hz from the 25 MHz internal oscillator (PRE_SCALE 3 to 255), or from EXTCLK up to 50 MHz Interface I2C up to 1 MHz (Fm+); 7-bit address 0x40 to 0x7F from A0 to A5; register auto-increment Outputs Totem pole (25 mA sink, 10 mA source at 5 V) or open drain; invertible; OE pin sets all to a chosen level Supply 2.3 V to 5.5 V; 5.5 V tolerant inputs and outputs What you get ¶ One object per chip. PCA9685<YourPort> takes a reference to your port and does no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . Switch-offs you can rely on. A switch-off is always sent, whatever the driver doubts, and Ok means the output is off; DisableOutputs() uses the OE pin, no bus needed. See Contract . Resets found. A power-on or software reset is found by its MODE1 sentinel, and the driver never writes its cached state over a reset chip. See Contract . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error such as Bus , DeviceReset or StateUnknown . See API guide . Datasheet defaults. Config{} holds the chip's reset values, with units in the field names, plus two presets for LEDs and servos. See Configuration . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class checked by a concept: the bus hooks and a delay, plus optional OE, failure and logging hooks found at compile time. See Porting . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . Tested without hardware. Host tests and a fuzzer run the driver against a register model of the chip that resets and sleeps on its own. See Testing and CI . API guide ¶ The driver's calls, task by task. Every example on this page is compiled by the host build from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp . Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP PCA9685 Rev. 4: MODE1, sleep, EXTCLK and the oscillator start-up: 7.3.1 Mode register 1, MODE1; Table 5, p. 14 Restart mode: 7.3.1.1 Restart mode, p. 15 LED output and PWM control, full ON and full OFF: 7.3.3 LED output and PWM control; Table 7; Figure 9, p. 16 ALL_LED registers and the orderly shutdown: 7.3.4 ALL_LED_ON and ALL_LED_OFF control; Table 8, p. 25 PWM frequency, PRE_SCALE: 7.3.5 PWM frequency PRE_SCALE; Equation 1, p. 25 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The shape of the API ¶ One object per chip: pca9685::PCA9685<Port> pwm(port, address, config) . The constructor does no I/O. Every call returns Result<T> : check ok() (or the bool conversion) before reading value ; on failure error says why and value is T{} . Channels are 0 to 15 (LED0 to LED15). A channel's value is a Pwm : the ON and OFF counts of the 12-bit counter (0 to 4095) and the full ON and full OFF bits. PwmOff() is the reset value; PwmForDuty(duty, phase) builds one from a duty in 4096ths. Calls with a trailing Verify verify = Verify::None can read back what they wrote: Verify::ReadBack costs two more reads (MODE1 and MODE2, then the channel) and returns WriteMismatch when the chip holds something else. Calls without I/O are Get...() and MayBeAsleep() ; everything else may touch the bus. Initialise ¶ pca9685 :: Error BringUp ( Pwm & pwm ) { // The one entry point: starts the chip on the first call, then returns Ok with no I/O. After a // failure the next call starts again from the beginning, switching every output off first. const auto r = pwm . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "PCA9685 init: %s 
 " , pca9685 :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } The first call switches every output off, writes and reads back the configuration and wakes the oscillator: thirteen transfers and a 500 µs wait. Once started, a call runs the reset check (one read) and starts again only when the chip reset; call it again after DeviceReset . Set a channel ¶ Call Writes Notes SetDuty(ch, duty, phase) on at phase , off duty counts later 0 is off, kFullDuty (4096) full ON; wraps into the next period (section 7.3.3, example 2) SetPulseWidthUs(ch, us) on at 0, off after us Uses the programmed PRE_SCALE; returns the programmed width in ns SetFullOn(ch) LEDn_ON_H bit 4 SetChannelOff(ch) LEDn_OFF_H = 0x10, one data byte Never refused; works also after a reset was found SetPwm(ch, value) the four registers of value ; an off value as one byte Equal ON and OFF counts without a full bit are refused (section 7.3.4) A switch-on is one 4-byte transfer from LEDn_ON_L, with auto-increment; the four bytes reach the output together at the STOP. A switch-off is the one byte LEDn_OFF_H = 0x10: stored or not, never part-way, and full OFF takes precedence over the rest, so a failed switch-off never makes a channel more active. Phases spread the switching edges of many channels and the supply current with them. Servos ¶ pca9685 :: Error CentreServos ( Pwm & pwm ) { // ServoPreset(): 50 Hz. Pulse widths use the programmed prescaler and Config::oscillator_hz. for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < 4 ; ++ ch ) { const auto r = pwm . SetPulseWidthUs ( ch , 1500 ); // returns the programmed width in ns if ( ! r ) { return r . error ; } } return pca9685 :: Error :: Ok ; } With ServoPreset() (50 Hz, PRE_SCALE 121) one count is 4.88 µs, so 1.5 ms is 307 counts; the call returns 1 498 160 ns, what was programmed. A width that rounds to 0 counts or to more than 4095 is InvalidArgument , never clamped. The internal oscillator is 25 MHz typical: calibrate Config::oscillator_hz for accurate pulses ( Hardware ). Set many channels at once ¶ pca9685 :: Error RgbTogether ( Pwm & pwm , uint16_t r , uint16_t g , uint16_t b ) { // One transfer: with OCH = 0 (the default) the three channels change together at the STOP. // Staggered phases spread the switching edges (section 7.3.3). const std :: array < pca9685 :: Pwm , 3 > rgb { pca9685 :: PwmForDuty ( r , 0 ). value , pca9685 :: PwmForDuty ( g , 1365 ). value , pca9685 :: PwmForDuty ( b , 2730 ). value }; return pwm . SetChannels ( 0 , rgb ). error ; // a bad value: switch-ons refused, switch-offs sent } SetChannels(first, values) sends its off values first, one byte each, then writes up to 16 consecutive channels in one transfer, so they change together at its STOP. SetChannelsOff(mask) switches off every channel of a 16-bit mask, one transfer each, and keeps going after a failure. SetAllOff() writes ALL_LED_OFF_H = 0x10: every channel off with one data byte (figure 24). Change the frequency ¶ SetPwmFrequency(hz) runs the data sheet's sequence: the reset check, SLEEP (the outputs hold for that moment), PRE_SCALE, a read-back of PRE_SCALE, the wake with its 500 µs wait, the wake check and RESTART when channels were running (sections 7.3.1.1, 7.3.5). The counts of each channel stay as they are, so pulse widths scale with the period: write them again. GetPwmFrequencyHz() returns the frequency of the programmed PRE_SCALE, which equation 1 rounds: 1000 Hz programs 1017 Hz (PRE_SCALE 5). Sleep and wake ¶ Call What happens Sleep() or Sleep(SleepMode::OutputsOff) Every channel off (ALL_LED), then MODE1.SLEEP: the safe low-power state. Wake() leaves every channel off. Sleep(SleepMode::HoldOutputs) MODE1.SLEEP with the channels as they are; RESTART sets. While asleep an output may hold its level, so a switch-off then returns Asleep . Wake() The reset check, SLEEP = 0, 500 µs, the wake check, then RESTART = 1 when it reads 1: the channels that ran before run again. Asleep, channel writes reach the registers, not the outputs (table 5, note 4); the calls return Asleep . Use DisableOutputs() for an immediate switch-off while asleep. Switch everything off now ¶ void EmergencyStop ( Pwm & pwm ) { // OE first: a pin write, no I2C, within 60 ns. Then every channel off over I2C. if ( auto r = pwm . DisableOutputs (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "OE: %s 
 " , pca9685 :: ToString ( r . error )); } if ( auto r = pwm . SetAllOff (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "ALL_LED off: %s 
 " , pca9685 :: ToString ( r . error )); } } DisableOutputs() drives OE high: every output goes to the off level within 60 ns, with no bus traffic, in any state. SetAllOff() then switches the channels off, so EnableOutputs() later does not turn them back on. EnableOutputs() is refused ( StateUnknown ) while any channel is unknown after a failed write. Find a reset ¶ pca9685 :: Error Supervise ( Pwm & pwm ) { // Once per control period: a reset the driver has not seen leaves every channel off and the // chip asleep, and the channel calls cannot tell (the chip acknowledges them). const auto r = pwm . CheckForReset (); if ( r . error == pca9685 :: Error :: DeviceReset ) { return pwm . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // then write the channels again } return r . error ; } CheckForReset() is one 3-byte read of MODE1, MODE2 and SUBADR1 (about 90 µs at 400 kHz); reset evidence is confirmed by a second read before the driver acts on it. A chip that reset is asleep with every channel off, and channel writes cannot tell; call it once per control period where the supply can dip. Contract has the rule. Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( pca9685 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case pca9685 :: Error :: Bus : case pca9685 :: Error :: NoDevice : case pca9685 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "check SDA, SCL, the pull-ups, VDD and the A0 to A5 address" ; case pca9685 :: Error :: DeviceReset : return "the chip reset (supply dip): EnsureInitialized() again" ; case pca9685 :: Error :: StateUnknown : return "a write failed: read the channel back or write it again" ; case pca9685 :: Error :: Asleep : return "written; the outputs follow after Wake()" ; default : return pca9685 :: ToString ( e ); } } Error What happened What to do NotInitialized Not started, or a reset was found EnsureInitialized() InvalidArgument An argument or a Config field is out of range; nothing sent Fix the value Bus A NACK or a bus error; the write may have arrived Retry the call; the channels it covered are unknown until then NoDevice Nothing acknowledged the address Check the wiring and the address DeviceIdMismatch Something answered that is not a PCA9685 Check the address and the part DeviceReset The chip reset (supply dip, software reset) EnsureInitialized() , then write the channels again InvalidReply A read the chip cannot send: a stuck or floating line Check SDA, the pull-ups, other parts on the bus Asleep Written; the outputs follow after Wake() Wake() , or DisableOutputs() for an immediate off StateUnknown A failed write left a value unknown; nothing sent ReadChannels() or ReadPrescale() , or write it again WriteMismatch The chip kept something else than was written Retry; check for noise ExternalClockLatched EXTCLK is set on the chip Power-cycle the chip, or configure the external clock Unsupported The port has no GpioSet() for OE Add the hook, or do without OE Diagnostics ¶ Call I/O Returns GetChannel(ch) none The copy of the channel; StateUnknown after a failed write GetUncertainChannels() none The channels whose last write failed ReadChannel(ch) , ReadChannels() reset check, then one read What the chip holds, into the copy GetPrescale() , GetPwmFrequencyHz() none The programmed prescaler and frequency ReadPrescale() reset check, then one read PRE_SCALE as the chip holds it ReadRegister(address) one read, no check Any register 0x00 to 0x45 or PRE_SCALE GetLastMode1() , GetLastMode2() none MODE1 and MODE2 as last read MayBeAsleep() none Whether the chip is or may be asleep Shut down ¶ void PowerDown ( Pwm & pwm ) { if ( auto r = pwm . Deinitialize (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "PCA9685 shutdown write failed: %s 
 " , pca9685 :: ToString ( r . error )); } } Deinitialize() drives OE high, switches every channel off and puts the chip to sleep (2.2 µA typical), then marks the driver uninitialised, even when a write failed.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: three layers, one of them yours, and what happens inside the calls that matter most. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP PCA9685 Rev. 4: Control register: 7.2 Control register, p. 9 Register summary and auto-increment: Table 4 Register summary, p. 10 LED output and PWM control, full ON and full OFF: 7.3.3 LED output and PWM control; Table 7; Figure 9, p. 16 I2C bus transactions: 9 Bus transactions; Figures 20 to 24, p. 32 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries under Breaking need source changes in code that used the affected API. [Unreleased] ¶ Changed ¶ The repository moved to kokeb-labs-drivers; URLs follow. [0.1.0] - 2026-11-10 ¶ Added ¶ Driver. pca9685::PCA9685<Port> for the NXP PCA9685 16-channel, 12-bit PWM controller (data sheet Rev. 4): header-only C++20, no heap, exceptions or RTTI, every call returning Result<T> . Start-up from any state. EnsureInitialized() switches every output off first (OE high, ALL_LED_OFF_H before and after MODE2 with OCH = 0), sets SLEEP and AI, EXTCLK by the two-write sequence, PRE_SCALE and the SUBADR1 reset sentinel, reads back MODE1, MODE2, SUBADR1, PRE_SCALE and every channel as the identity check, wakes the oscillator with its 500 µs wait, checks the wake and enables OE. It refuses the LED All Call address 0x70 and clears ALLCALL and the Sub Call enables. Once started, a later call runs the reset check instead of returning at once. Channels. SetPwm() , SetDuty() with a phase delay, SetPulseWidthUs() from the programmed prescaler, SetFullOn() , SetChannelOff() , SetChannels() (up to 16 in one transfer), SetChannelsOff() , SetAllOff() ; a switch-on writes its four registers in one transfer, applied at the STOP; a switch-off is one data byte, LEDn_OFF_H or ALL_LED_OFF_H = 0x10, so even a failed switch-off never makes a channel more active; bank calls send their switch-offs first; Verify::ReadBack on the single-channel calls. Frequency, sleep and restart. SetPwmFrequency() by sleep, PRE_SCALE, read-back, wake and RESTART; Sleep(SleepMode::OutputsOff) and Sleep(SleepMode::HoldOutputs) ; Wake() with the RESTART sequence. Output enable. DisableOutputs() and EnableOutputs() through the optional GpioSet() hook; the driver chooses MODE2.OUTNE so that OE high always gives the level of a channel that is off. Resets. A power-on or software reset is found by MODE1.AI = 0, or MODE2, EXTCLK, SUBADR1 (a sentinel no MODE1 write can mask) or PRE_SCALE back at its reset value, confirmed by a second read ( DeviceReset , CheckForReset() ); acting on it drives OE high and writes ALL_LED_OFF_H. MODE1 is never written from the copy over a reset chip, every write that clears SLEEP is followed by the wake check, and EnableOutputs() checks first. Once started, the switch-offs keep working after a reset was found, and Deinitialize() always does its work: OE high first, which needs no bus, and nothing at all on an address the start-up refuses (0x70, LED All Call). Stuck lines. A reserved bit set is InvalidReply ; a channel read of all zeros, which SDA stuck low also gives, is data only when one more MODE1/MODE2/SUBADR1 read matches the running chip. Failed writes. A switch-on or burst that failed may have arrived: channels and the prescaler become unknown ( GetUncertainChannels() , StateUnknown ); switch-ons that depend on them are refused, switch-offs never are, and a bank call that refuses its switch-ons still sends its switch-offs. Configuration. Config with the reset values, Validate() , CheckedConfig , ServoPreset() , DirectLedPreset() , PrescaleFor() , FrequencyFor() , CountsForPulseUs() , PulseNsForCounts() , PwmForDuty() ; Kconfig options for ESP-IDF. Port. I2cInterface and the I2cPort concept, bus requirements ( kI2cAddress , kMaxClockHz , kRepeatedStart ), optional GpioSet() , GetLastFailure() and Log() hooks; the host port and two ESP-IDF ports, OE on a GPIO and OE tied to VSS. Tests. A register model written from the data sheet that resets, sleeps and restarts on its own and offers both readings of each open question; host tests for every call and failure path, including a NACK at every byte of every switch-off and a reset before every transfer of a session; a fuzz target whose invariants are the safety rules (a switch-off never makes a channel more active), with its corpus. docs.text: Configuration ¶ pca9685::Config holds everything EnsureInitialized() writes to the chip. Its defaults are the chip's reset values, so Config{} describes a chip that was just reset. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP PCA9685 Rev. 4: MODE1, sleep, EXTCLK and the oscillator start-up: 7.3.1 Mode register 1, MODE1; Table 5, p. 14 MODE2, output drive, inversion, change on STOP, OUTNE: 7.3.2 Mode register 2, MODE2; Table 6, p. 16 PWM frequency, PRE_SCALE: 7.3.5 PWM frequency PRE_SCALE; Equation 1, p. 25 External drivers, INVRT and OUTDRV: 7.7 Using the PCA9685 with and without external drivers; Table 12; Figures 13 to 15, p. 29 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Fields ¶ Field Default (reset value) Register Range pwm_frequency_hz 200 PRE_SCALE = round(oscillator / (4096 x f)) - 1, 0x1E PRE_SCALE 3 to 255: about 24 Hz to 1526 Hz at 25 MHz (section 7.3.5) oscillator_hz 25 000 000 (none: the arithmetic) 1 MHz to 50 MHz; the internal oscillator is 25 MHz typical clock ClockSource::Internal MODE1.EXTCLK External is sticky until a power cycle or software reset (table 5) output_drive OutputDrive::TotemPole MODE2.OUTDRV OpenDrain for LEDs with Zener diodes (section 10, question 5) invert_outputs false MODE2.INVRT true for loads wired active low (table 12) What the driver sets itself: Register bits Value Why MODE1.AI 1 Bursts of up to 64 bytes; the reset sentinel ( Contract ) MODE1.ALLCALL, SUB1 to SUB3 0 No group address can change the chip behind the driver MODE2.OCH 0 Every byte of one transfer reaches the outputs together at the STOP ( Contract ) MODE2.OUTNE the off level OE high always switches the outputs off ( Hardware ) The frequency follows equation 1 with rounding: the frequency the chip runs at is oscillator / (4096 x (PRE_SCALE + 1)) , which GetPwmFrequencyHz() returns and FrequencyFor() computes offline. 200 Hz programs 197 Hz, 50 Hz programs 50 Hz, 1000 Hz programs 1017 Hz. Presets ¶ Preset For Differs from Config{} ServoPreset() Hobby servos, external N-type drivers 50 Hz DirectLedPreset() LEDs wired from the supply into the outputs (figure 15) 1000 Hz, open drain, inverted DirectLedPreset() wires a load active low: after a chip reset it is lit until EnsureInitialized() runs again ( Hardware ). pca9685 :: Config ZenerLedConfig () { pca9685 :: Config c {}; // the reset values: 200 Hz, totem pole c . output_drive = pca9685 :: OutputDrive :: OpenDrain ; // LEDs with Zener diodes (section 10, Q5) c . pwm_frequency_hz = 1000 ; // PRE_SCALE 5 c . oscillator_hz = 25'000'000 ; // or the measured value of this board return c ; // pca9685::Validate(c) checks it offline } pca9685 :: Error StartLeds ( MyPort & port ) { static pca9685 :: PCA9685 < MyPort > pwm ( port , 0x41 , ZenerLedConfig ()); // A0 high; no I/O return pwm . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // InvalidArgument if the config is out of range } Validation ¶ Validate(config) checks a configuration without the chip: every enumeration holds an enumerator, the oscillator is in range, the frequency is 1 Hz to kMaxPwmFrequencyHz and its prescaler 3 to 255. EnsureInitialized() and ApplyConfig() run it before any I/O and return InvalidArgument . A value is never clamped. docs.text: Contract ¶ What the PCA9685 driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP PCA9685 Rev. 4: LED All Call and Sub Call addresses: 7.1.2 LED All Call I2C-bus address; 7.1.3 LED Sub Call I2C-bus addresses, p. 8 Register summary and auto-increment: Table 4 Register summary, p. 10 MODE1, sleep, EXTCLK and the oscillator start-up: 7.3.1 Mode register 1, MODE1; Table 5, p. 14 Restart mode: 7.3.1.1 Restart mode, p. 15 MODE2, output drive, inversion, change on STOP, OUTNE: 7.3.2 Mode register 2, MODE2; Table 6, p. 16 ALL_LED registers and the orderly shutdown: 7.3.4 ALL_LED_ON and ALL_LED_OFF control; Table 8, p. 25 SUBADR1, the reset sentinel: 7.3.6 SUBADR1 to SUBADR3; Table 9, p. 26 Output enable, OE: 7.4 Active LOW output enable input; Table 11, p. 27 Power-on reset: 7.5 Power-on reset, p. 27 Software reset by the general call: 7.6 Software reset, p. 28 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration and the address, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. Its first call checks the configuration and the address ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, switches every output off first (OE high, ALL_LED_OFF_H, MODE2 with OCH = 0, ALL_LED_OFF_H again, each sent even if one before it failed), then writes MODE1, PRE_SCALE and the SUBADR1 sentinel, reads MODE1, MODE2, SUBADR1, PRE_SCALE and all 16 channels back (the identity check), wakes the oscillator, waits 500 µs, checks the wake and enables OE. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again from the beginning. Once started, a later call is not a shortcut: it runs the reset check (one 3-byte read), returns Ok when the chip kept its state, and starts again from the beginning when it reset. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before the first EnsureInitialized() succeeds, except Deinitialize() (below) and DisableOutputs() (a pin write). No call initialises the chip as a side effect. ApplyConfig() before the start only stores the configuration. Every port failure propagates, as Bus , or as NoDevice when the port's GetLastFailure() reports an address NACK; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read. A reply a floating, stuck or shared line can produce is never data: a reserved bit set (MODE2 bits 7 to 5, SUBADR1 bit 0, bits 7 to 5 of an _H channel byte) is InvalidReply ; MODE1 with AI clear is reset evidence. Equal ON and OFF counts with no full bit are a value (the output is never asserted, figure 9): a switch-on NACKed part-way can leave them, so one such channel does not fail a read of all 16. A channel read of all zeros, which SDA stuck low also gives, counts only once a second frame agrees: one more MODE1/MODE2/SUBADR1 read must match the running chip, or the read is InvalidReply and leaves every channel in doubt as it was. The only wait is the oscillator start-up, kOscillatorStartUs (500 µs, the data sheet maximum) after every wake from the internal oscillator. No call polls. Config{} equals the reset values of MODE1, MODE2 and PRE_SCALE (except that the driver clears ALLCALL and sets AI, and SUBADR1 holds the sentinel). A missing DelayUs() is a compile error; a missing GpioSet() gives Unsupported from DisableOutputs() and EnableOutputs() ; a missing GetLastFailure() reports every failure as Bus ; a missing Log() logs nothing. A misdeclared hook is a compile error. Deinitialize() always does its work, whatever the driver believes (never started, started, or a reset found), on an address EnsureInitialized() accepts; any other is InvalidArgument with no I/O (0x70 is LED All Call at power-up, where the writes would reach every PCA9685). It drives OE high first, which needs no bus, then brings the bus up and sends ALL_LED_OFF_H, then, only when that switch-off was sent (asleep, an output still on would be held on), a wake first when an output may be held and MODE1.SLEEP. It returns Ok only when all of that was sent; the driver is uninitialised afterwards either way. Switch-offs ¶ One data byte. Every switch-off is sent as a single data byte: 0x10 to LEDn_OFF_H (register 0x06 + 4n + 3 ), or 0x10 to ALL_LED_OFF_H (figure 24). One byte is stored or it is not, and full OFF takes precedence over everything else the channel holds (table 7 remark). A 4-byte burst NACKed part-way would leave new ON bytes with the old OFF bytes, applied at the STOP (section 7.3.2, note 2): a phase-shifted channel could end up nearly 100 % on. So no switch-off ever makes a channel more active, even when it fails. Never refused. A channel call with an off value ( full_off set, SetDuty(n, 0) , SetPulseWidthUs(n, 0) , SetChannelOff() ), SetChannelsOff() , SetAllOff() , DisableOutputs() and Sleep(SleepMode::OutputsOff) 's first write are sent whatever the driver doubts: an unknown channel, an unknown prescaler, a pending wake check. Once the driver has started, they are sent also while it is uninitialised after a reset was found or Deinitialize() . An off request is never InvalidArgument (only a channel number above 15 is). Every one, first. A bank call sends each off value as its single byte before any burst; it still sends them when it refuses its switch-ons (an invalid value, a failing wake check). SetChannelsOff() keeps going after a failed write. Ok means off. Ok from a switch-off means the channel's output is off on the chip. While the chip may be asleep holding its outputs (after Sleep(SleepMode::HoldOutputs) , or a wake that was not confirmed), the write is sent and the call returns Asleep : asleep, no output can be switched on or off (table 5, note 4), so DisableOutputs() (OE high, at once) or Wake() completes it. No shortcut. No call skips a write because the driver's copy says it is not needed. Writes that may or may not have arrived ¶ A switch-off byte that failed left the channel as it was, or off: the copy keeps the riskier "as it was"; nothing becomes unknown. A switch-on or a bank burst whose transfer failed with Bus may have reached the chip, in whole or in part: with OCH = 0 the bytes acknowledged before a NACK reach the outputs at the STOP (section 7.3.2). The channels it covered become unknown ( GetUncertainChannels() ); GetChannel() returns StateUnknown for them and EnableOutputs() refuses while any is unknown. A successful write, a switch-off, ReadChannel() or ReadChannels() makes them known again. A failed PRE_SCALE write makes the prescaler unknown; SetPulseWidthUs() refuses ( StateUnknown , nothing sent) until a successful SetPwmFrequency() , ReadPrescale() or wake check. PRE_SCALE ignores writes while awake (table 4, note 1), which the chip still acknowledges: SetPwmFrequency() always reads it back and returns WriteMismatch when it did not take. NoDevice (an address NACK) proves nothing arrived: nothing becomes unknown. The driver keeps MODE2.OCH = 0. With OCH = 1 a channel changes only when "all 4" of its registers are loaded (section 7.3.2, note 3), and which bytes count after a NACK is not specified. Resets ¶ A power-on reset (VDD below V_POR) or a software reset (the general call 0x06 ) loads every reset value: MODE1 = 0x11, asleep with AI clear; every channel full OFF; MODE2 = 0x04; SUBADR1 = 0xE2; PRE_SCALE = 0x1E; EXTCLK clear (sections 7.5, 7.6). The sentinels. The driver sets MODE1.AI and never clears it, and writes MODE2, EXTCLK and SUBADR1 only at start-up (SUBADR1 = 0x5A , inert while MODE1.SUB1 = 0, table 9). Every reset check reads MODE1, MODE2 and SUBADR1 in one 3-byte burst; AI = 0, or MODE2, EXTCLK or SUBADR1 different from the copy, is reset evidence. SUBADR1 is the one no MODE1 write of the driver can mask, so a reset is found even when MODE2 and PRE_SCALE equal their reset values ( Config{} ). Two frames decide. Reset evidence is confirmed by a second read before the driver acts (handbook rule 12d); a single corrupted read is an error ( InvalidReply ) or a glitch the second read clears, never a reset. Acting on it. The call drives OE high, writes the single-byte ALL_LED_OFF_H, marks the driver uninitialised and returns DeviceReset . The switch-off calls and Deinitialize() keep working from there. Read before a cached write. Sleep() , Wake() and SetPwmFrequency() read MODE1, MODE2 and SUBADR1 before they write MODE1 from the copy; CheckForReset() , EnsureInitialized() on a started driver and EnableOutputs() read them too; Verify::ReadBack , ReadChannel() , ReadChannels() and ReadPrescale() read them first (a burst read needs AI). A reset the driver has not seen leaves the chip asleep, and asleep no output can switch on. Channel calls keep returning Ok then (the chip acknowledges their writes; with AI clear they land in one register), so call CheckForReset() where a supply dip is possible. Never run on reset values. The driver wakes the chip only by a MODE1 write with SLEEP = 0 (the wake, and the RESTART write, which clears SLEEP too), and every such write is followed by the wake check: MODE1, MODE2, SUBADR1 and PRE_SCALE read and compared with the copy. A check that fails stays pending: the next call runs it first, and a switch-on is refused until it passes. Two frames for a state change. Only an acknowledged wake write followed by a check that reads SLEEP = 0 clears the doubt that an output may be held; a read alone never does. Active-low loads. After a reset every output is low and not inverted. A load wired active high is off; one wired active low is on until EnsureInitialized() runs again ( Hardware ). Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates pca9685_version.h Your port The bus, within the bus requirements; the delay; optionally OE, at its inactive level (high) before the first transfer, the failure reason and logging ( Porting ) Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the org. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state. Another master on the bus must not write to the chip: the driver's copy would not know. Errors ¶ pca9685::Error inside pca9685::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; this driver returns NotInitialized , InvalidArgument , Bus , DeviceIdMismatch and Unsupported from it, plus seven chip-specific values. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, or Deinitialize() ran or a reset was found since (switch-offs still go out once started) InvalidArgument 2 A Config field, the address or an argument is out of range; nothing was sent (a bank call still sends its switch-offs), also by Deinitialize() Bus 3 A port hook returned false : a data NACK, a bus error, an OE pin write Timeout , Crc , Busy , DeviceFault 4, 6, 7, 8 Never returned DeviceIdMismatch 5 At start-up, a register did not read back what was written: no PCA9685, or another part Unsupported 9 DisableOutputs() or EnableOutputs() without GpioSet() WriteMismatch 16 A read-back differs: Verify::ReadBack , PRE_SCALE in SetPwmFrequency() , SLEEP still set after Wake() NoDevice 17 An address NACK, with GetLastFailure() DeviceReset 18 The chip reset since the start, confirmed by two reads; OE high, every channel off, the driver uninitialised InvalidReply 19 A read returned what no PCA9685 can send (a reserved bit set, or an inconsistent MODE1/MODE2/SUBADR1 frame), or a channel read of all zeros the MODE1/MODE2/SUBADR1 read did not confirm Asleep 20 Written, but the chip is or may be asleep: the outputs do not follow until Wake() StateUnknown 21 The call depends on a value a failed write left unknown; nothing was sent ExternalClockLatched 22 MODE1.EXTCLK is set but the internal clock is asked for The API guide says what to do about each. Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, the address, a Config , the copy of the 16 channels and a few flags: 144 bytes on a 64-bit host. The largest stack buffers are one burst of all 16 channels: 64 bytes, and 65 in the register helper's frame. Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ None.

Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, or Deinitialize() ran or a reset was found since (switch-offs still go out once started) InvalidArgument 2 A Config field, the address or an argument is out of range; nothing was sent (a bank call still sends its switch-offs), also by Deinitialize() Bus 3 A port hook returned false : a data NACK, a bus error, an OE pin write Timeout , Crc , Busy , DeviceFault 4, 6, 7, 8 Never returned DeviceIdMismatch 5 At start-up, a register did not read back what was written: no PCA9685, or another part Unsupported 9 DisableOutputs() or EnableOutputs() without GpioSet() WriteMismatch 16 A read-back differs: Verify::ReadBack , PRE_SCALE in SetPwmFrequency() , SLEEP still set after Wake() NoDevice 17 An address NACK, with GetLastFailure() DeviceReset 18 The chip reset since the start, confirmed by two reads; OE high, every channel off, the driver uninitialised InvalidReply 19 A read returned what no PCA9685 can send (a reserved bit set, or an inconsistent MODE1/MODE2/SUBADR1 frame), or a channel read of all zeros the MODE1/MODE2/SUBADR1 read did not confirm Asleep 20 Written, but the chip is or may be asleep: the outputs do not follow until Wake() StateUnknown 21 The call depends on a value a failed write left unknown; nothing was sent ExternalClockLatched 22 MODE1.EXTCLK is set but the internal clock is asked for The API guide says what to do about each.

docs.text: No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, the address, a Config , the copy of the 16 channels and a few flags: 144 bytes on a 64-bit host. The largest stack buffers are one burst of all 16 channels: 64 bytes, and 65 in the register helper's frame.

LED n is channel n of the driver: SetDuty(n, ...) . Blocks ¶ Figure 1 of the data sheet, which draws one output for clarity; here the 16 outputs are split over two blocks. Inside the PCA9685 Figure description and sources The PCA9685's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp . Address ¶ The 7-bit address is 1 A5 A4 A3 A2 A1 A0 (figure 4): 0x40 ( kI2cAddress ) with every pin low, up to 0x7F . The address pins have no internal pull-ups (section 7.1.1): tie each one to VDD or VSS, never leave one open. A5 A4 A3 A2 A1 A0 Address 000000 0x40 000001 0x41 110000 0x70 : not usable, see below 111111 0x7F Every PCA9685 also acknowledges the LED All Call address, 0x70 , from power-up until MODE1.ALLCALL is cleared (section 7.1.2). A chip strapped to 0x70 would share it with every other PCA9685 on the bus, so the driver refuses that address ( InvalidArgument , no I/O). EnsureInitialized() clears ALLCALL and the three Sub Call enables, so once started the chip answers only its own address. The general call address 0x00 with the byte 0x06 resets every PCA9685 on the bus (section 7.6); the driver never sends it, and finds the reset it causes. Output enable (OE) ¶ OE low lets the outputs follow their channels; OE high sets every output to the MODE2.OUTNE level within 60 ns (section 7.4, table 15). The driver chooses OUTNE so that OE high always gives the level of a channel that is off: Config Channel off at the pin OUTNE OE high at the pin not inverted ( invert_outputs = false ) low 00 low inverted, totem pole high 01 high inverted, open drain high impedance 10 high impedance So DisableOutputs() (OE high) is the fast switch-off: a pin write, no bus traffic, and it works asleep or with the bus down. Wire OE to a GPIO with a pull-up to VDD (10 kΩ): the outputs stay disabled until the MCU drives OE low, through MCU reset and boot. The data sheet's figure 26 shows the pull-up as needed when the MCU's OE drive is open drain. Without the GPIO, tie OE to VSS and leave out the port's GpioSet() . OE can also dim or blink every output together with an external PWM on it (section 7.4); the driver does not use that, but it does not stop it either. EXTCLK ¶ The PWM counter runs from the internal oscillator, 25 MHz typical, or from EXTCLK, DC to 50 MHz (table 15). EXTCLK must be grounded when it is not used (table 3, note 2). Select it with Config::clock = ClockSource::External and Config::oscillator_hz set to its frequency; the start-up sets MODE1.EXTCLK by the two-write sequence of table 5. EXTCLK then stays set until a power cycle or a software reset: a later start with the internal clock returns ExternalClockLatched . An external clock needs no start-up wait, and it lets several PCA9685 run in step. The internal oscillator is specified only as 25 MHz typical, so the PWM period and every pulse width are only as accurate as it is. For servo work, measure the period on one output once and set Config::oscillator_hz to 4096 x (PRE_SCALE + 1) / period ( not verified on hardware : bench step 4 in Testing and CI ). I2C bus ¶ Setting Value Source Address 0x40 to 0x7F , not 0x70 figure 4, section 7.1.2 SCL Standard (100 kHz), Fast (400 kHz) or Fast-mode Plus (1 MHz) table 15 Reads Control register write, repeated START, read ( kRepeatedStart ) figure 22 Bus time-out The chip resets its bus interface when SDA or SCL is held low for 25 ms or more table 15, note 1 SDA and SCL need pull-ups to the bus supply (section 8): choose them for the bus capacitance and speed by the I2C specification, UM10204 section 7 (figure 26, note 1). As a start, 4.7 kΩ suits 100 kHz and 400 kHz on a short bus; Fast-mode Plus needs stronger pull-ups, which the SDA output's 30 mA sink allows (section 2). Reference application circuit ¶ Figure 26 of the data sheet: an I2C master with SDA and SCL pull-ups, OE on a GPIO with a 10 kΩ pull-up, EXTCLK and A0 to A5 strapped, and the 16 outputs driving LED strings from 5 V or 12 V through external transistors. Its remark sets INVRT = 0, OUTDRV = 1, OUTNE = 01 for that circuit; the driver's Config{} matches it except OUTNE, which the driver makes 00 so that OE high switches the strings off rather than on. The schematic below is the part of figure 26 that has no transistors, with one LED on LED0; parts the figure gives no value for are marked as not confirmed. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp . docs.text: The 7-bit address is 1 A5 A4 A3 A2 A1 A0 (figure 4): 0x40 ( kI2cAddress ) with every pin low, up to 0x7F . The address pins have no internal pull-ups (section 7.1.1): tie each one to VDD or VSS, never leave one open. A5 A4 A3 A2 A1 A0 Address 000000 0x40 000001 0x41 110000 0x70 : not usable, see below 111111 0x7F Every PCA9685 also acknowledges the LED All Call address, 0x70 , from power-up until MODE1.ALLCALL is cleared (section 7.1.2). A chip strapped to 0x70 would share it with every other PCA9685 on the bus, so the driver refuses that address ( InvalidArgument , no I/O). EnsureInitialized() clears ALLCALL and the three Sub Call enables, so once started the chip answers only its own address. The general call address 0x00 with the byte 0x06 resets every PCA9685 on the bus (section 7.6); the driver never sends it, and finds the reset it causes.

docs.text: OE low lets the outputs follow their channels; OE high sets every output to the MODE2.OUTNE level within 60 ns (section 7.4, table 15). The driver chooses OUTNE so that OE high always gives the level of a channel that is off: Config Channel off at the pin OUTNE OE high at the pin not inverted ( invert_outputs = false ) low 00 low inverted, totem pole high 01 high inverted, open drain high impedance 10 high impedance So DisableOutputs() (OE high) is the fast switch-off: a pin write, no bus traffic, and it works asleep or with the bus down. Wire OE to a GPIO with a pull-up to VDD (10 kΩ): the outputs stay disabled until the MCU drives OE low, through MCU reset and boot. The data sheet's figure 26 shows the pull-up as needed when the MCU's OE drive is open drain. Without the GPIO, tie OE to VSS and leave out the port's GpioSet() . OE can also dim or blink every output together with an external PWM on it (section 7.4); the driver does not use that, but it does not stop it either.

docs.text: The PWM counter runs from the internal oscillator, 25 MHz typical, or from EXTCLK, DC to 50 MHz (table 15). EXTCLK must be grounded when it is not used (table 3, note 2). Select it with Config::clock = ClockSource::External and Config::oscillator_hz set to its frequency; the start-up sets MODE1.EXTCLK by the two-write sequence of table 5. EXTCLK then stays set until a power cycle or a software reset: a later start with the internal clock returns ExternalClockLatched . An external clock needs no start-up wait, and it lets several PCA9685 run in step. The internal oscillator is specified only as 25 MHz typical, so the PWM period and every pulse width are only as accurate as it is. For servo work, measure the period on one output once and set Config::oscillator_hz to 4096 x (PRE_SCALE + 1) / period ( not verified on hardware : bench step 4 in Testing and CI ).

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( pca9685_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-pca9685.git external/driver-pca9685 git submodule update --init external/driver-pca9685 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-pca9685 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE pca9685::pca9685 ) pca9685::pca9685 is an alias of the pca9685 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect PCA9685_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver PCA9685_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-pca9685 -B build-pca9685 cmake --install build-pca9685 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( pca9685 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE pca9685::pca9685 ) The target is pca9685::pca9685 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated pca9685_version.h go to include/pca9685/inc/ , the template implementation to include/pca9685/src/pca9685.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-pca9685) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-pca9685 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-pca9685.git components/pca9685 pca9685 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml pca9685 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : pca9685 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-pca9685.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES pca9685 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/pca9685_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into pca9685_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = pca9685 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port. Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP PCA9685 Rev. 4: Slave address, A0 to A5: 7.1.1 Regular I2C-bus slave address; Figure 4, p. 7 Output enable, OE: 7.4 Active LOW output enable input; Table 11, p. 27 I2C bus transactions: 9 Bus transactions; Figures 20 to 24, p. 32 I2C timing, EXTCLK and OE propagation: 13 Dynamic characteristics; Table 15, p. 40 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from pca9685::I2cInterface<Self> (in inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the pca9685::I2cPort concept, so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false makes the driver's EnsureInitialized() return Bus bool Write(uint8_t addr, const uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) noexcept yes START, addr + W, len bytes, STOP. false on a NACK or any bus error; send the STOP after a NACK too bool WriteRead(uint8_t addr, const uint8_t* tx, std::size_t tx_len, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t rx_len) noexcept yes START, addr + W, tx , repeated START, addr + R, rx_len bytes (NACK the last), STOP void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes Wait at least us microseconds: the 500 µs oscillator start-up bool GpioSet(CtrlPin, GpioSignal) noexcept no Drive OE; false if the pin write failed bool GetLastFailure(I2cFailure& failure) noexcept no After Write() or WriteRead() returned false : set failure and return true when the controller knows why void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string addr is the 7-bit address the driver was constructed with; shift it yourself if your SDK wants the 8-bit form. The port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public pca9685 :: I2cInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One write transaction: START, address + W, the bytes (register first), STOP. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( addr , data , len ); } // Write then read with a repeated START in between. bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the 500 us oscillator start-up depends on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the transfers must follow: One call, one transaction. The register address is the first byte of Write() and the tx of WriteRead() ; never split a burst. The driver writes up to 65 bytes (all 16 channels) and reads up to 64 in one transaction, relying on auto-increment, which does not carry over a STOP. A STOP after a NACK. With MODE2.OCH = 0 the chip applies the bytes it acknowledged at the STOP; the driver counts on the STOP to know what may have reached the outputs. Repeated START for WriteRead() , no STOP between the write and the read (figure 22). Raw bytes only. Do not retry: a retried write can repeat a change the driver already counted as sent, and a retried read hides a fault. The driver owns the framing. Bounded time-outs. A stuck bus fails the call; it does not block forever. The chip resets its own bus interface after SDA or SCL is held low for 25 ms (table 15, note 1). A bus clear before a retried start-up. After a bus error, clock SCL nine times with SDA released (or use your SDK's bus recovery) before the application calls EnsureInitialized() again (handbook KB-HW-019). Bus requirements ¶ The driver states what the PCA9685 needs from the bus as constexpr values in inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port's settings against them with static_assert , as both example ports do: Constant Value Meaning Data sheet kI2cAddress 0x40 7-bit address with A5 to A0 low; the pins add 0 to 63 (0x40 to 0x7F, not 0x70) 7.1.1, figure 4 kMaxClockHz 1'000'000 Standard, Fast or Fast-mode Plus 13, table 15 (f_SCL) kRepeatedStart true A register read is one write-read with a repeated START 9, figure 22 inline constexpr uint32_t kMyClockHz = 400'000 ; static_assert ( kMyClockHz <= pca9685 :: kMaxClockHz , "SCL above the PCA9685's maximum" ); static_assert ( pca9685 :: kRepeatedStart , "WriteRead() must use a repeated START" ); NACKs. The chip NACKs reserved register addresses (0x46 to 0xF9) and the general call with a byte other than 0x06 ; the driver sends neither. The NACK the master sends on the last byte it reads ends the read; it is not a failure. A NACK the port reports is therefore always a fault: no chip at the address ( NoDevice with GetLastFailure() , Bus without it) or a data byte refused ( Bus ). The driver never probes with an empty or zero-length transfer: every transfer carries the register address (handbook KB-CPP-130). Control pins ¶ Each control pin has a defined idle level, and the port drives it there before it enables the pin's output and before the driver's first transfer (handbook KB-HW-018). Configuring a pin as an output first and setting its level afterwards gives the chip a pulse it did not ask for: here, a moment of enabled outputs. CtrlPin Package pin Polarity Idle ( INACTIVE ) level Before the first transfer OutputEnable OE (TSSOP28 23, HVQFN28 20) active low high: every output at the off level Set high, then enable the output GpioSignal::ACTIVE always means "function asserted", here "outputs enabled", which is a low level on the pin. The driver drives OE INACTIVE as its first step of EnsureInitialized() and ACTIVE as its last, and again in DisableOutputs() and EnableOutputs() . A board with OE tied to VSS needs no hook. The address pins and EXTCLK are strapped on the board, not driven by the port. Optional hooks ¶ The driver finds the optional hooks at compile time with C++20 requires , in one place ( pca9685::detail ). A missing hook falls back in a documented, safe way or fails to compile; it never skips a step silently. Hook Used for Without it DelayUs() The 500 µs oscillator start-up after every wake Compile error at the first call that waits GpioSet() OE: EnsureInitialized() , DisableOutputs() , EnableOutputs() , Deinitialize() OE must be tied low; the two calls return Error::Unsupported GetLastFailure() Telling an address NACK ( NoDevice , nothing arrived) from a data NACK ( Bus , part of the write may have arrived) Every failure is Bus , and the driver treats the write as possibly delivered Log() One line per lifecycle event or failure Nothing is logged A port with every hook: class FullPort : public pca9685 :: I2cInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { // Drive OE high (outputs disabled) before the pin becomes an output (KB-HW-018). return platform_gpio_write ( kOeGpio , true ) && platform_i2c_init (); } bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( addr , data , len ); // STOP also after a NACK } bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len ); } // Required: the 500 us oscillator start-up after a wake. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: OE on a GPIO. ACTIVE means "outputs enabled", which is a low level on the pin. bool GpioSet ( pca9685 :: CtrlPin pin , pca9685 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { if ( pin != pca9685 :: CtrlPin :: OutputEnable ) { return false ; } return platform_gpio_write ( kOeGpio , signal == pca9685 :: GpioSignal :: INACTIVE ); } // Optional: tells an address NACK (nothing there: NoDevice) from a data NACK (Bus). bool GetLastFailure ( pca9685 :: I2cFailure & failure ) noexcept { failure = platform_i2c_last_was_address_nack () ? pca9685 :: I2cFailure :: AddressNack : pca9685 :: I2cFailure :: Other ; return true ; } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( pca9685 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > pca9685 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kOeGpio = 7 ; }; pca9685 :: Error FastOff ( pca9685 :: PCA9685 < FullPort >& pwm ) { // With GpioSet() this drives OE high; a port without it gets Error::Unsupported. return pwm . DisableOutputs (). error ; } A GpioSet() that returns void is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write. The compile-fail tests check this and the other hook rules. Reference implementations ¶ Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_pca9685_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated chip. Start from it for a host build or a test bench; it is also the smallest complete port. examples/esp32/main/esp32_pca9685_port.hpp : ESP-IDF, with every hook. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that writes, bursts and repeated-START reads work, since the start-up reads back every register it wrote. Call SetDuty(0, 2048) and measure LED0: a square wave at 197 Hz typical ( Config{} ), 50 % duty. With OE on a GPIO: DisableOutputs() takes LED0 to the off level at once; EnableOutputs() brings it back. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several chips share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract . Editor setup ¶ The clang-format and clang-tidy configuration is in _config/ , and the repository root has no copy of it. Tools that take a path use it directly; CI does the same: Tool Setting Command line clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy -p build VS Code (C/C++ extension) "C_Cpp.clang_format_style": "file:${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-format" and "C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args": ["--config-file=${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-tidy"] clangd (VS Code clangd, Neovim, Emacs), CLion These find .clang-format and .clang-tidy only by name, from the file upwards: copy both to the root once ( cp _config/.clang-format _config/.clang-tidy . ). .gitignore lists the copies, so they never reach a commit; copy again after _config/ changes Configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON (clangd: --compile-commands-dir=build ) so the editor sees the same flags as the build.

Datasheet sections this page relies on From NXP PCA9685 Rev. 4: Pins and packages (TSSOP28, HVQFN28): 6 Pinning information; Table 3 Pin description, p. 6 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated PCA9685, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/pca9685_host_example PCA9685 driver 0.1.0 on the host pca9685: initialised PWM 50 Hz (PRE_SCALE 121) LED0 duty 0/4096 LED0 duty 1024/4096 LED0 duty 2048/4096 LED0 duty 3072/4096 LED0 duty 4096/4096 servo on LED1: 1498160 ns pulse The calls in main.cpp are the ones below; only the port differs on an MCU. CI builds and runs this example on every pull request. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU PCA9685 (TSSOP28 pin) Notes I2C SCL SCL (26) Pull-up to VDD; 4.7 kΩ suits 100 kHz and 400 kHz I2C SDA SDA (27) Pull-up to VDD GND A0 to A5 (1 to 5, 24) Address 0x40 ( kI2cAddress ); the pins have no pull-ups, never leave one open GND EXTCLK (25) Must be grounded when the internal oscillator is used GND OE (23) Outputs always enabled for this example 3.3 V or 5 V VDD (28) 2.3 V to 5.5 V; 100 nF to VSS close to the pin GND VSS (14) LED0 (6) LED anode, cathode through 330 Ω to GND Driven high by the totem-pole output The Hardware page has every pin of both packages, OE wired to a GPIO, servos, open-drain LEDs and the power. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the pca9685::pca9685 CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-pca9685.git external/driver-pca9685 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: it brings the bus up, moves bytes and waits. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public pca9685 :: I2cInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One write transaction: START, address + W, the bytes (register first), STOP. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write ( addr , data , len ); } // Write then read with a repeated START in between. bool WriteRead ( uint8_t addr , const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the 500 us oscillator start-up depends on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method, the optional hooks and the transfer rules. 4. Dim the LED ¶ main.cpp #include "pca9685.hpp" int dim_led_to_quarter ( MyPort & port ) { pca9685 :: PCA9685 < MyPort > pwm ( port ); // address 0x40 (A5..A0 low), Config{}: no I/O yet if ( auto r = pwm . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. every channel off, configured, oscillator on return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Bus or DeviceIdMismatch: check wiring and address } if ( auto r = pwm . SetDuty ( 0 , 1024 ); ! r ) { // 2. LED0 on for 1024 of 4096 counts, 200 Hz return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); } return static_cast < int > ( pwm . SetChannelOff ( 0 ). error ); // 3. off again: never refused } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() calls your port's EnsureInitialized() , switches every output off whatever state the chip was left in, writes Config{} (the reset values: 200 Hz, totem pole, not inverted), reads it back to prove a PCA9685 answers, and wakes the oscillator with its 500 µs start-up wait. SetDuty(0, 1024) writes LED0's four registers in one transfer: on at count 0, off at count 1024 of 4096. SetChannelOff(0) sets LED0's full OFF bit. A switch-off is never refused. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns Bus Nothing acknowledged 0x40: SDA, SCL, the pull-ups, VDD, A0 to A5 ( Troubleshooting ) EnsureInitialized() returns DeviceIdMismatch Something answered that is not a PCA9685, or SDA is stuck EnsureInitialized() returns ExternalClockLatched EXTCLK is set on the chip from an earlier run: power-cycle it The calls return Ok but the LED stays dark OE is high, or the LED's polarity needs invert_outputs ( Troubleshooting ) Next ¶ API guide : servos, banks of channels, the frequency, sleep and resets. Configuration : presets, every Config field, Kconfig. Examples : the host example and the MCU examples. Platforms : which MCUs have a port and an example.

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply , and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --public --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-<chip> # the plan: every setting that would change python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, security, Actions, rulesets, labels A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md .
